description: A global fashion brand sells articles of clothing in several markets. We have an estimate of how price changes affect sales for each article, assuming constant price elasticity. Price changes must be in multiples of 1 euro. Initial prices for each article are given, and no more than a certain fraction of the prices can change. The new price for each article must be within an allowed range of the initial price. Each article has a maximum production volume; we cannot sell more than that. Given the sales forecast per article for the next twelve months and past elasticities, the goal is to choose new prices for each article to maximize expected revenue.

A company manufactures several types of products and utilizes various raw materials in the production process. The company has a specific amount of each type of raw material available. Each product requires a certain amount of each raw material for every unit produced and generates a specific amount of revenue per unit. The challenge for the company is to determine the optimal quantity of each product to produce to maximize total revenue.

- Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC) has introduced new families of \var{N} computer systems with different memory, disk storage, and expansion capabilities.
- Each system \var{i} is either a general-purpose (GP) system or a workstation (WS) system.
- Each system \var{i} can have an integer number of disk drives, and on average \var{disk_i} units of disk drive per system are requested by customers for system \var{i}.
- System \var{i} uses \var{mem_i} units of 256K memory boards per system on average.
- System \var{i} has a price of \var{price_i} dollars.
- The in-house supplier of CPUs for DEC could provide at most \var{max_cpu} units, due to debugging problems.
- The supply of disk drives is uncertain and is estimated by the manufacturer to be in the range of \var{min_disk} to \var{max_disk} units.
- the supply of 256K memory boards is also limited in the range of \var{min_mem} to \var{max_mem} units.
- Maximum demand for system \var{i} in the next quarter is estimated to be \var{demand_i} units.
- Maximum demand for the whole GP family in the next quarter is estimated to be \var{demand_GP} units.
- Maximum demand for the whole WS family in the next quarter is estimated to be \var{demand_WS} units.
- Included in the projections, there are \var{preorder_i} orders for system \var{i} that have already been received and have to be fulfilled in the next quarter.
- To address the shortage of 256K memory boards, DEC has access to \var{alt_mem} units of an alternative memory board that can only be used in certain systems.
- you can assume the number of systems produced is a floating point number to make the problem easier to solve.

description:
A state is planning its electricity capacity for the next several years. The state has a forecast of the demand for electricity each year, which is presumed to be accurate. Currently, there are existing oil-fired power plants that will continue to operate and provide some of the needed electricity.
To meet the growing demand, the state is considering building either coal-fired or nuclear power plants. Building coal plants costs a certain amount per unit of capacity, and similarly, building nuclear plants has its own cost per unit of capacity.
However, there are limitations. For political and safety reasons, the state has decided that nuclear power should not exceed a certain percentage of the total electricity capacity. Additionally, coal plants have a certain lifespan, after which they will no longer be operational, and the same goes for nuclear plants.
The goal is to figure out the most cost-effective plan to expand electricity capacity by deciding how much to invest in coal and nuclear plants each year, while adhering to the constraints on nuclear power and considering the lifespan of each type of plant.

A hospital needs to create a weekly schedule for its nurses working the night shift from 12 PM to 8 AM. The demand for nurses during the night shift varies each day of the week. For each day, there is a specific number of nurses required.
Each nurse works for a certain number of consecutive days on the night shift, followed by several days off, ensuring they have a balanced work-rest schedule over the week. The challenge is to determine the minimum number of nurses the hospital needs to hire to meet the varying daily demands for the night shift throughout the week.

Consider a communication network made up of several nodes. These nodes are connected by communication links that allow one-way transmission of data from one node to another. Each link between nodes has a specific capacity, meaning it can carry a certain number of bits per second, and there is a cost associated with transmitting data along each link. 
Each node in the network generates data that needs to be sent to another specific node. This data can be sent directly or by passing through several intermediate nodes. Additionally, data from the same origin to the same destination can be split up and sent through different paths.
The goal is to determine the paths that all data should take to reach their intended destinations, while keeping the total transmission cost as low as possible.

Consider a rocket that travels along a straight path. Let x_t, v_t, and a_t be the position, velocity, and acceleration, respectively, of the rocket at time t.
By discretizing time and by taking the time increment to be unity, we obtain an approximate discrete-time model of the form 
    
    x_{t+1} = x_t + v_t
    v_{t+1} = v_t + a_t

We assume that the acceleration a_t is under our control, as it is determined by the rocket thrust. In a rough model, the magnitude |a_t| of the accelera­tion can be assumed to be equal to the rate of fuel consumption at time t. 
Suppose that we have x_0 and v_0 as the initial position and velocity, respectively, of the rocket. We wish the rocket to take off and reach a target position x_T with speed v_T at time T. Furthermore, we wish to accomplish this in an economical fashion, that is, by using as little fuel as possible.

    v_{t+1} = v_t + a_t

- We assume that the acceleration a_t is under our control, as it is determined by the rocket thrust.

- Suppose that we have x_0 and v_0 as the initial position and velocity, respectively, of the rocket.
- We wish the rocket to take off and reach a target position x_T with speed v_T at time T.
- The goal is to achieve this with the least pressure on the passengers, minimizing the maximum thrust required.

A small firm specializes in making some types of spare automobile parts. Each part has to go through several machines. We know the required worker-hours for each part on each machine. We also know the profit made on each part. Each machine has a capacity in terms of worker-hours. The firm wants to determine how many of each part to make in order to maximize profit.

We have a random variable Z that takes values 0, 1, ..., K with probabilities p_0, p_1, ..., p_K, respectively. We are given the values of the first two moments:

E[Z] = \sum_{k=0}^{K} k p_k
E[Z^2] = \sum_{k=0}^{K} k^2 p_k

We would like to obtain a lower bound on the value of the fourth moment:

E[Z^4] = \sum_{k=0}^{K} k^4 p_k

Use linear programming to find a lower bound on E[Z^4].

There is a road divided into a number of segments, and we want to illuminate it using a number of lamps. Each lamp has a certain power, and the illumination of each segment is equal to sum of the powers of all lamps, multiplied by some known coefficients. We are given the desired illumination of each segment, and we want to choose the powers of the lamps so that the illuminations are as close to the desired illuminations as possible.

Consider a school district with a number of neighborhoods, schools, and grades at each school. Each school has a capacity for each grade. In each neighborhood, the student population of each grade is known. The distance of each school from each neighborhood is also known. The goal is to assign all students to schools, while minimizing the total distance traveled by all students.

A company must deliver Deliver_i units of its product at the end of the i-th month. Material produced during a month can be delivered either at the end of the same month or can be stored as inventory and delivered at the end of a subsequent month. There is a storage cost of StorageCost dollars per month for each unit of product held in inventory. The year begins with zero inventory. If the company produces x_i units in month i and x_{i+1} units in month i+1, it incurs a cost of SwitchCost |x_{i+1} - x_i| dollars, reflecting the cost of switching to a new production level. Assume that inventory left at the end of the year has no value and does not incur any storage cost. The company wants to minimize the total cost of the production and inventory schedule over the next T months.

An office supply company makes two types of printers: color printers and black and white printers. Different sections of the factory with different teams produce each printer. The color printer team can produce at most MaxColorPrinters per day while the black and white printer team can produce at most MaxBWPrinters per day. Both teams require use of the same paper tray installing machine and this machine can make at most MaxMachineCapacity printers of either type each day. Color printers generate a profit of ProfitColorPrinter per printer while black and white printers generate a profit of ProfitBWPrinter per printer. How many of each printer should be made to maximize the company's profit?

An accounting firm has senior accountants earning SeniorWage per week and junior accountants earning JuniorWage per week. The contracts with companies to provide accounting services require at least MinTotalAccountants accountants, of whom at least MinSeniorAccountants must be senior accountants. To make sure there is enough experience on the accounting team, the number of senior accountants should be at least one third of the number of junior accountants. The firm wants to keep the weekly wage bill below WageBillLimit. Formulate an LP to minimize the wage bill.

A farmer has TotalAcres available for growing apples and pears. The farmer must allocate at least MinApplesAcres to apples and at least MinPearsAcres to pears. The profit per acre of apples is ProfitPerAcreApples and the profit per acre of pears is ProfitPerAcrePears. Additionally, the total acreage used for apples and pears combined should not exceed TotalAcres, and the farmer can grow at most MaxPearsToApplesRatio times the amount of pears as apples. How many acres should be allocated to each fruit to maximize profit, and what is that maximum profit?

A lighting company makes two types of lamps: desk-lamps and night-lamps. There is an expected demand of at least DemandDeskLamps desk-lamps and DemandNightLamps night-lamps each day. However, due to the size of their factory, they can make at most MaxDeskLamps desk-lamps and MaxNightLamps night-lamps per day. To satisfy a contract, a minimum of MinTotalLamps lamps must be made each day. The profit per desk-lamp sold is ProfitDeskLamp and the profit per night-lamp sold is ProfitNightLamp. The objective is to determine the number of desk-lamps and night-lamps to maximize profit while meeting demand and contract requirements.

An investor wants to allocate TotalInvestment amount of money between the telecom and healthcare industries. The amount invested in telecom should be at least MinTelecomHealthcareRatio times the amount invested in healthcare and should not exceed MaxTelecomInvestment. The investment in telecom yields TelecomInterestRate, while the investment in healthcare yields HealthcareInterestRate. The objective is to maximize the total profit from the investments.

A farmer has TotalHectares available to grow tomatoes and potatoes. She prefers to plant more tomatoes than potatoes, but the soil and weather conditions allow her to grow at most MaxTomatoesToPotatoesRatio times the amount of tomatoes to that of potatoes. In addition, she must grow at least MinTomatoes hectares of tomatoes and at least MinPotatoes hectares of potatoes to meet community demands. If the profit per hectare of tomatoes is ProfitPerHectareTomatoes and the profit per hectare of potatoes is ProfitPerHectarePotatoes, how many hectares of each crop should she plant to maximize profit? What is this profit?

A audio company makes two types of headphones: wired headphones and wireless headphones. Two different teams make each type of headphone. The wired team can make at most MaxWiredProduction wired headphones per day and the wireless team can make at most MaxWirelessProduction wireless headphones per day. Both teams require use of a shared audio testing machine, and this machine can be used to make a maximum of MaxTestingCapacity headphones per day. The profit per wired headphone is ProfitWired and the profit per wireless headphone is ProfitWireless. How many of each headphone should be made to maximize profit?

Jacob has TotalInvestment to invest. He has decided to invest in his favorite clothing company and his favorite tech company. He has decided that the money invested in his favorite clothing company must be at least ClothingToTechRatio times as much as the amount invested in his favorite tech company. He has also limited himself to invest at most MaxTechInvestment in his favorite tech company. If the money invested in his favorite clothing company earns ClothingInterestRate and the money invested in his favorite tech company earns TechInterestRate, how much should he invest in each to maximize his profit?

Each month a store owner can spend at most MaxExpenditure on carrots and cucumbers. A carrot costs the store owner CostCarrot and a cucumber costs the store owner CostCucumber. Each carrot is sold for a profit of ProfitCarrot and each cucumber is sold for a profit of ProfitCucumber. The owner estimates that the number of cucumbers sold is at most CucumberFraction of the number of carrots sold. He also estimates that at least MinCarrots but at most MaxCarrots are sold each month. How many of each, carrots and cucumbers, should be sold in order to maximize the profit?

A farmer wants to manufacture a special plant nutrition using two types of fertilizers, A and B. Each kg of fertilizer A contains NitrogenA units of nitrogen, PhosphoricAcidA units of phosphoric acid, VitaminAA units of vitamin A, and VitaminDA units of vitamin D. Each kg of fertilizer B contains NitrogenB units of nitrogen, PhosphoricAcidB units of phosphoric acid, VitaminAB units of vitamin A, and VitaminDB units of vitamin D. The plant nutrition must meet a minimum requirement of MinNitrogen units of nitrogen and MinPhosphoricAcid units of phosphoric acid, and must not exceed MaxVitaminA units of vitamin A. The goal is to determine the amount of each fertilizer that minimizes the total amount of vitamin D in the nutrition.
